title: Grandmother Amanda and his mixed ancestry
summary: Callender corrects himself on his grandmother's name and lists the Indian, Scottish and Ashanti strands of his heritage.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Before we get started, I'd like to add something. When we were here on Reel 1, we were talking about my grandmother, and for the life of me, I couldn't think of her name. Well, her name was Amanda, and they called her Mandy.
Do you know what her maiden name was?

Tolls, I believe. She was half-Indian. I don't know whether it was Cherokee or whatever was common to Virginia, but she was half-Indian with high cheekbones and all. So I have all kind of Indian in me -- American Indian, West Indian, East Indian...

Yeah. Well, I didn't mention that before, that the Scotsmen who came to the island in 1700 also married African women, and it happened to be the Ashanti. So whatever they are, I'm a part of that, too.
And you found that out through the genealogy that you said you had?
I found that out through the genealogy.
